title: Check if it is Possible to Split Array
summary: Given an array nums of length n and an integer m, determine if it's possible to split nums into n arrays of size 1 by repeatedly splitting arrays of length at least two into two good arrays, where a good array has a length of 1 or a sum of elements ≥ m.
statement: Given an array nums of length n and an integer m, determine if it's possible to split nums into n arrays of size 1 by repeatedly splitting arrays of length at least two into two good arrays, where a good array has a length of 1 or a sum of elements ≥ m.
constraints: Repeatedly split arrays until singletons remain; every non-singleton part created must have sum at least m.
Return whether a complete sequence of valid splits exists.
reference_solution:
def can_split_array(nums,m):
    return len(nums)<=2 or any(a+b>=m for a,b in zip(nums,nums[1:]))
hints: A valid process exists exactly when a length-two core can survive until the final split.
Arrays of length at most two always work; otherwise find an adjacent pair with sum at least m.
Scan adjacent sums and return whether one reaches the threshold.
Keep that pair together while peeling off outside singleton elements; conversely every valid process has such a final pair.
editorial: Keep that pair together while peeling off outside singleton elements; conversely every valid process has such a final pair.

tests.explanation: The adjacent pair 2+2 reaches four and can anchor a valid split sequence.
No adjacent pair reaches five, so no valid first-to-last splitting sequence exists.
